old_caption:
The video captures a serene sky scene, where the primary focus is on the dynamic interplay between clouds and sunlight. The sky is a gradient of blue hues, transitioning from a lighter shade near the horizon to a deeper blue higher up. Scattered throughout the sky are various formations of clouds, ranging from fluffy white cumulus clouds to denser, darker gray formations. These clouds move slowly across the frame, creating a sense of gentle motion.

As the video progresses, beams of sunlight pierce through the gaps in the clouds, casting radiant rays that illuminate parts of the sky and create a dramatic contrast against the darker areas. These sunbeams shift slightly, suggesting the movement of the clouds or the angle of the sun. The interplay of light and shadow adds depth and texture to the scene, enhancing its visual appeal.

In the upper part of the frames, a small dark object, likely a bird, appears and moves across the sky, adding a subtle point of motion. The scene remains largely static otherwise, with the clouds and light rays being the main elements of change.

caption:
The video captures a bright blue sky where crepuscular sunbeams fan upward from behind a central cumulus cloud mass near the lower edge. Darker cloud wisps sit along the lower-left and lower-right margins. The beams keep a steady number and broad spread, and their brightness looks broadly constant. The cloud and ray arrangement appears to shift slowly upward across the view, with the cloud top rising gradually into the open sky.

A small dark bird silhouette drifts into view near the top center and moves on a diagonal path toward the right side of the sky. Its shape briefly shows outstretched wings as it travels across the open blue. It remains a tiny dark mark, descending gradually from the upper region toward the mid-right, then drifting slightly lower and left while staying visible.

A few faint additional specks appear intermittently in the mid-sky, while the steady beams and the slow upward drift of the cloud remain the dominant backdrop in the open sky.

The first view may already be mid-action; the last view need not contain completion. Different
endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.

'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.
